introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-001
items.detail: Design a secure access-control and network-monitoring system for university research laboratories containing sensitive equipment and research data.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: The system should allow only authorized students, faculty, researchers, and lab administrators to access designated lab networks and systems based on role and approved permissions.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003
items.detail: Administrative users should be able to grant or revoke access, review active sessions, monitor unusual login activity, and receive alerts for repeated failed authentication, unauthorized access attempts, and access outside approved lab hours.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: The system should maintain audit logs of access decisions and administrator actions, isolate research lab networks from general student and guest networks, and support both university-managed and approved research devices.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-005
items.detail: The solution should be secure, reliable, and manageable across multiple research buildings.

glossary.summary: Source-present terminology; definitions introduce no additional product obligation.

items.title: Access control
items.detail: Rules and enforcement governing which principals may perform actions on resources.

items.title: Audit record
items.detail: A stored record of an event. Required event scope and retention are determined by the linked source, not this definition.

items.title: Log
items.detail: A collection of event records. This term does not itself require additional logging fields, events or access permissions.

items.title: Device isolation
items.detail: Restriction of a device's network access; the source determines whether and by whom this action is permitted.

sdlc.justification: The selection of Agile as the required model is based on a uniform score of 40 across all candidates, with no differentiating input evidence provided to favor one methodology over another. Given the absence of explicit factors such as budget, delivery timelines, failure consequences, feedback mechanisms, legacy systems, regulation, schedule constraints, stability needs, uncertainty levels, or verification requirements, no candidate model can be objectively ranked for suitability. The provisional nature of this decision reflects an incomplete evidence base. All models receive equal score meaning—suitability points out of 100—not probabilities. Without evidence to differentiate between Agile and other methodologies (e.g., DevSecOps, Spiral, V-Model, Waterfall, Hybrid, Incremental), the choice remains arbitrary and unsupported by input data. The requirement for secure access control, role-based permissions, real-time monitoring, audit logging, and cross-building manageability aligns with iterative development principles but does not inherently mandate Agile over other models. Unknown factors such as regulation or legacy systems could influence model selection if addressed; however, these are currently unaccounted for in the input evidence. Therefore, this decision is grounded only in equal suitability scores and lacks evidentiary differentiation.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
